title: Parking lot design
idea: A parking lot design matches each vehicle to a free spot of the right size, issues a ticket on entry, and prices the stay on exit.

analogy.text: A cloakroom attendant hangs your coat on a hook that fits, hands you a numbered tag, and returns the coat when you show it.
analogy.breaks: A cloakroom rarely sorts hooks by size or charges by the hour.

points: Nouns in the requirements become classes: lot, floor, spot, vehicle, ticket, gate.
One ordered `Size` enum compares vehicles with spots in a single line.
`ParkingLot` alone allocates spots; gates only call it, so rules live once.
Pricing sits behind a `FeeRule` interface, so a new tariff needs no edits.

hero.title: From entry gate to exit gate

edges.label: park(vehicle)
edges.caption: A vehicle arrives. The gate asks `ParkingLot` for a spot; the gate itself holds no parking rules.

edges.label: search
edges.caption: The lot walks its floors in order and asks each one for a free spot that fits.

edges.label: smallest fit
edges.caption: The smallest free spot that fits wins, so large spots stay free for large vehicles.

edges.label: issue
edges.caption: The lot marks the spot taken and returns a `Ticket` with plate, spot and entry time.

edges.label: fee(hours)
edges.caption: On exit the gate asks the configured `FeeRule` for a price. It never knows which rule it holds.

edges.label: leave(ticket)
edges.caption: After payment the gate calls `leave`, and the spot is free for the next vehicle.

code.title: Allocate spots
code.caption: One flat floor of three spots. Two cars arrive, a bus waits, then a spot frees up. Entry time is left out to keep it short.

walk.text: An enum and three records carry the data. Records have no setters.
`ParkingLot` owns the spots and a map of which spot ids are taken.
Keep free spots the vehicle fits, then pick the smallest by enum order.
`synchronized`: two gates calling at once cannot both win one spot.
Mark the spot taken and return a ticket. An empty `Optional` means full.
`leave` frees the spot named on the ticket.
Two medium vehicles arrive, a bus is turned away, then retries after one leaves.

code.title: Price the stay
code.caption: Three tariffs behind one interface. The lot would call `fee` without asking which one it holds.

walk.text: `FeeRule` is the pricing contract; a default method gives each rule a name.
Each tariff is a small `record` that carries its numbers as data.
`main` prices a short and a long stay under every rule.

pitfalls: Lock allocation: two gates calling `park` together must never get one spot.
Skip a subclass per vehicle type when only its size changes behaviour.
Keep tariffs out of `Ticket` and `ParkingLot`; prices change more often than spots.

quiz.q: What is the second line `ParkingLotDemo` prints?
quiz.why: The car took M1 and S1 is too small for a medium van. The only free spot that fits is L1.

takeaway: Nouns become classes; one owner allocates; pricing is a swappable strategy.

starters: How would I add floors and a display board of free spots?
Should electric-vehicle charging spots be a new size or a separate flag?
How do I keep allocation fast when the lot has thousands of spots?
